First, let's rewrite the polynomial equation in the form ${P}_{n}(q)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}5{q}^{5}-7{q}^{4}+10{q}^{3}-6q & =-{q}^{5}+11{q}^{4}-2{q}^{3}-6q \\ 6{q}^{5}-18{q}^{4}+10{q}^{3}-6q & =-2{q}^{3}-6q \\ 6{q}^{5}-18{q}^{4}+12{q}^{3} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Next, notice that all of the terms of the polynomial have a common factor of $6{q}^{3}.$ We can factor out the $6{q}^{3}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}6{q}^{5}-18{q}^{4}+12{q}^{3} & =0 \\ 6{q}^{3}({q}^{2}-3q+2) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we factor the expression ${q}^{2}-3q+2$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}6{q}^{3}({q}^{2}-3q+2) & =0 \\ 6{q}^{3}(q-1)(q-2) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, by applying the zero product rule, the solutions are $q=0,$ $q=1,$ and $q=2.$

Therefore, using the zero product rule, we have that the solutions are $0,\,1$ and $2.$
